text: How long does probate take in Queensland? Here's a quick guide from Catton Roderick Lawyers. No Queensland law sets a total time for probate. The notice of intention to apply must be given at least fourteen days before filing. Then the registry checks the papers, with no set time. A caveat, or a missing original will, can hold up the grant. And the Public Trustee says finishing an estate usually takes an average of twelve months. If you're an executor, our team can help.
